messages.subject: Re: Compilation problem in TMB with surplus production
messages.subject_clean: Compilation problem in TMB with surplus production
messages.body_plain:
Hi Ellie

The first things I'd check are: whether you've navigated into the directory with the .cpp file from R, and whether there are any lingering .o and/or .so files hanging around. I always have a `system('rm model.o model.so')` call in my R code before I compile.

All that being said, I have been able to get TMB to pick up the cpp file in my `TMB::compile` call, but the compilation fails because it's acting up on the `posfun` function. It's almost likely that CppAD and tmbutils are having some kind of Type conflicts looking at the stack trace, but I don't know enough about the CppAD and tmbutils namespace to conclude that (Kasper might be able to shed light on this better). I don't understand what `posfun` is doing with the `CondExpGe` call, but if the main purpose is for you to force `P(t+1)` to be positive, then you could maybe look up other ways of doing so?

I'm gonna run this through with some of my colleagues who can TMB real good, and also I'm super interested in your model as well, because I need to start writing up a state space model myself in the future probably! I'll update you if I find something fruitful!

Nafis

messages.body_plain:
For models without random effects it is possible to  evaluate the Hessian

obj <- MakeADFun(data=dat, parameters=pars)
H = obj$he()

but data.class(H) is "matrix", and not one of the sparse matrix classes in R.

Is it possible to access H in sparse form?

messages.subject: Re: How to access a sparse hessian in non-RE models?
messages.subject_clean: How to access a sparse hessian in non-RE models?
messages.body_plain:
You can overload 'he' with its sparse version like this:

obj$env$random <- seq_along(obj$par)   ## Fake all parameters are random
obj$he <- TMB:::sparseHessianFun(obj)   ## Overload hessian function
obj$env$random <- NULL ## Restore random

Now obj$he() is sparse.

messages.subject: feenableexcept crashes R
messages.body_plain:
I have a model which I can fit using nlminb, but with optim it errors out with message

Error in iterate(par) :

Newton dropout because inner gradient had non-finite components.

Error in optim(par = c(55, 253, 0.17, -4, 4.7, 14.4, 0.93, 2, 0.48, -1.3 :

L-BFGS-B needs finite values of 'fn'

Trying to find out what was causing non-finite values I followed the advice here <http://kaskr.github.io/adcomp/_book/Errors.html#floating-point-exception> and added lines

#include <fenv.h>

and

feenableexcept(FE_INVALID | FE_OVERFLOW | FE_DIVBYZERO | FE_UNDERFLOW);

to my cpp code and tried again.

This wasn't helpful: it caused R to crash with error

Process R floating point exception (core dumped) at Wed Jun 27 11:00:58 2018

This is not the same as the above error because (a) it occurred in an earlier point of the run, and (b) I got the same crash whether I used nlminb or optim.  The crash doesn't happen if I comment out the feenableexcept line.

gdb didn't help to locate the cause of this crash.  I ran gdb manually, as suggested here <https://github.com/kaskr/adcomp/issues/254> with

R -d gdb  => run => source("run.R")

The crash produced the Arithmetic exception error

Program received signal SIGFPE, Arithmetic exception.

0x00007ffff7937fcb in ?? () from /usr/lib/R/lib/libR.so

and bt produced a whole bunch of output referring to libR.so and ending with

#31 0x00007ffff71e8830 in __libc_start_main (main=0x4007b0 <main>, argc=1,

argv=0x7fffffffde48, init=<optimized out>, fini=<optimized out>,

rtld_fini=<optimized out>, stack_end=0x7fffffffde38)

at ../csu/libc-start.c:291

#32 0x0000000000400809 in _start ()

which I can't understand (to start with I can't find libc-start.c).

I'd be grateful for any suggestions about my two problems: (a) I can't locate the cause of the original Newton dropout error above; and (b) I don't know why feenableexcept crashes R with my model.

All the runs I mention above can be made with the attached files by

1. Either leaving in, or commenting out, line 14 of AMSFc.cpp (the feenableexcept line)

2. Setting the last argument in the last line of run.R to 'optim' or 'nlminb'

3. Typing source('run.R') in an R session.
